tagline: A desert loop through the moon-training country.
intro: East of Tonopah, the loop leaves US 6 near mile marker 79 and runs into a volcanic field of cinder cones and basalt flows. The road is unpaved and bumpy. Easy Chair Crater appears early on the drive; farther along comes Lunar Crater, with a stopping place near its rim.
This dry, rugged country has served as a training ground for astronauts and a testing ground for prototype Mars rovers. The lunar name acquired some practical use.

moments.title: Easy Chair Crater
moments.text: One of the first craters visible from the byway, Easy Chair has a parking place at its foot.

moments.title: Lunar Crater
moments.text: From the rim parking area, the ground falls into a volcanic crater about 430 feet deep.

practical: The loop is unpaved and calls for a high-clearance vehicle; vehicles are limited to existing roads and trails.
